name: Gupa
confidence_why: One first-hand description, checked against the source; 5 other works consulted do not discuss stress.
catalog_citation: Blench, Roger M. 2013. The Nupoid languages of West-Central Nigeria: overview and comparative wordlist. Working document, Cambridge, 14 March 2013, 141 pp. (self-published, rogerblench.info). Parallel: Blench, Roger M. 1989. Nupoid. In John Bendor-Samuel (ed.), The Niger-Congo languages, 305-322. Lanham MD: University Press of America.
catalog_locator: Blench 2013 §2.3 Tone, p. 8; tone-marking table p. 9; Gupa entry §1.3 item 7, pp. 2-3; tone-marked Gupa rows in the comparative wordlist (e.g. 'root' ágbèrè, item 3, p. 19; 'seed, stone, pip' akòkò, item 5, p. 21). Parallel wording Blench 1989 §14.3.3 Tone, pp. 314-315.
catalog_quote: All Nupoid languages presently studied have at least five surface tones, three level tones and two glides. This produces a possible five-way lexical contrast (for Nupe examples, see Madugu 1970). Nupe and Gbagye also have a lowered mid-tone at surface level, although in both cases this has been analysed as an allotone of the mid-tone (Smith 19xx). With the exception of loanwords and ideophones, these can all be analysed as three underlying level tones, with rising and falling tones as allotones of the level tones. Nupe, Gbari and Gade seem to exhibit downdrift, but do not have terraced tones. The tones are shown as follows; ... High ˊ Mid Unmarked Low ˋ Rising ˆ Falling ˇ
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

Nupe, Gbari and Gade seem to exhibit downdrift, but do not have terraced tones.") is verbatim in, §2.3 Tone, printed p. 8 = p. 10 (extracted text, 141-page A4 PDF, Acrobat Distiller 2013-03-14); the tone-marking scheme (High ˊ, Mid unmarked, Low ˋ, Rising ˆ, Falling ˇ) follows on printed p. 9 = p. 11. The Gupa entry (§1.3 item 7, printed pp. 2-3 = pp. 4-5: villages Gupa, Atsu, Kirikpo south of Lapai; Meek 1925 Gupa/Kupa confusion; 86% cognate with Dibo, 90% with Kami; retains seven vowels) reads as reported, and p. 2 states that Blench's own manuscript…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Gupa is treated as a three-level-tone language (H, M unmarked, L, plus rising and falling allotones), like every other Nupoid language; the source is a family-level generalization backed by Blench's own tone-marked Gupa and Abawa wordlists (1979-82). No statement about word stress exists in any source found.
new_statements.exceptions: Loanwords and ideophones may carry tones outside the three-level analysis (family-level remark, not Gupa-specific).
new_statements.domain_note: Family-level statement about Nupoid; Gupa is among the languages Blench collected wordlists for, and the Gupa/Abawa forms in the wordlist are tone-marked, but the sentence is not Gupa-specific. Stress is not discussed at word or phrase level.
new_statements.identity_note: Gupa-Abawa [gpa] = gupa1248; Ethnologue/Blench treat Gupa and Abawa as two dialects (Blench 2013 wordlist has separate Gupa and Abawa columns; Blench 1989 item 1 'Agbi' at Abugi-Jankara is a further related lect). Not to be confused with Kupa [kug] (kupa1238), a confusion Blench notes goes back to Meek 1925. The tone statement quoted is about Nupoid as a whole, not Gupa specifically.

sources.note: Nothing on stress. Gupa entry (§1.3 item 7, pp. 2-3): villages south of Lapai, 86% cognate with Dibo, 90% with Kami, retains seven vowels. §2.3 Tone (p. 8): 'All Nupoid languages presently studied have at least five surface tones, three level tones and two glides.. analysed as three underlying level tones'. Gupa and Abawa wordlist columns carry tone marks (ágbèrè, akòkò, akpárà, asùsù, táhũ̀, áʤwè). Data source: Blench's own manuscript wordlists of Gupa 1979-82 (p. 2).

sources.note: The only post-1989 first-hand field report covering Gupa (Gupa-Atsu, pp. 17-18 per Glottolog); a sociolinguistic survey with wordlists, so a stress statement is unlikely, but it may contain tone/phonology observations on the Nupe cluster and is the most recent primary data.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3, languoid gupa1248 and reference records 656700 (Decker & Abraham 2022) and 552883 (Weise 2013)
sources.note: No grammar or phonology listed (Glottolog lists no grammar, sketch or phonology). Decker & Abraham 2022 = Journal of Language Survey Reports 2022-021, pp. 1-57, typed sociolinguistic + wordlist, covering Gupa-Atsu = Gupa (pp. 17-18 per languoid page). Weise 2013 = UCLA history dissertation, wordlist/overview type, Gupa/Abawa pp. 97-106.

sources.note: Entry 162 Gupa-Abawa (p. 36, p. 64): Niger State, Lapai LGA around Gupa and Edzu; >10,000 Gupa and 5,000 Abawa (1989); dialects Gupa, Abawa; 'Source(s) Blench (1989)'. No phonology or grammar reference for Gupa-Abawa (the 'Grammar: Caron (2002)' printed beside it belongs to the adjacent right-column entry *Guus, South Bauchi Chadic). Nothing on tone or stress.
